references.text: God announces His covenant with Noah before the flood. This is the same covenant that is confirmed and expanded in Genesis 9:9.
The covenant from verse 9 is elaborated: God promises never again to destroy the earth with a flood, and the rainbow is set as a sign of the covenant.
God establishes His covenant with Abraham and his descendants as an everlasting covenant, reflecting the covenant pattern from Noah's covenant.
Isaiah explicitly refers to Noah's covenant and compares God's unchanging grace with the promise never to flood the earth again.
God promises a new covenant with Israel, which is part of the pattern of God's covenant promises throughout salvation history.
Jesus is described as the mediator of a better covenant, which builds upon and fulfills the earlier covenants, including Noah's covenant.
Connects the promise of fruitfulness and numerous descendants in the Noahic covenant with the Abrahamic covenant.
Shows how the blessings of the law in Leviticus are an elaboration of the original covenant promises regarding fruitfulness.
Links God's everlasting covenant with Noah to His everlasting covenant with Israel, emphasizing God's infinite faithfulness.
Demonstrates the structural similarity in the covenant concerning descendants between Noah and Abraham.
Refers directly to the ark as the symbol of the covenant established with Noah.
Shows the continuity of the covenant across generations, from Noah to Israel.
